title: 21.5 A Fully Integrated Multi-Phase Voltage Regulator with Enhanced Light-Load-Efficiency Peak of 86%, Featuring an Autonomous Mode Transition from Hard-Switching to Soft-Switching to Discontinuous Conduction Mode in 3nm FinFET CMOS
problem: Fully integrated voltage regulators (FIVRs) face efficiency challenges across the power spectrum: high efficiency at peak power (current surges) but poor efficiency at idle loads; soft-switching and DCM modes reduce ripple but degrade efficiency under high load.
motivation: Modern SoCs (especially AI-driven) demand localized power delivery with hundreds of Amperes; data centers require both peak-power and idle-state efficiency for cost-effective operation.
method: The design combines a power supply (voltage regulator) directly integrated into a 3nm chip that automatically switches its operating mode based on power demand. When the chip draws heavy current, it uses hard-switching—rapidly flipping transistors on and off to transfer power efficiently. At lower power levels, the system automatically switches to soft-switching (transistor transitions with less electrical noise) and then discontinuous conduction mode (where the inductor fully discharges each cycle, reducing noise further). This three-mode approach keeps voltage stable while achieving 86% efficiency when running at light load.
key_novelty: The key innovation is automatically switching between three operating modes—hard-switching at high load, soft-switching at medium load, and discontinuous conduction mode at light load—to maintain efficiency across the full power range.
contributions: Autonomous mode selection across load spectrum
Soft-switching and DCM for idle-power reduction
primary_theme: Multi-mode FIVR optimizing full-spectrum load efficiency
